indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.1.1 Analyse the relationships among and between 2-D shapes and 3-D objects according to a variety of attributes, including measurement
indicator.objective: Use cut-out paper as a square corner to determine angles which are right angles and angles which are not right angles

skills.description: Identify right angles using a square corner.
Sort angles into right angles and not right angles.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking a rotated right angle is not a right angle.
Relying on visual estimation instead of the square corner.

questions.stem: What is a right angle?
options: An angle that looks like a corner of a book.
An angle smaller than a square corner.
An angle greater than a square corner.
hints: It is exactly a quarter turn.
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly a quarter turn (90 degrees), like the corner of a square.
questions.misconception: Thinking any acute angle is right.

questions.stem: Does a square have right angles?
options: Yes, all 4 angles are right angles.
Only some of its angles are right angles.
questions.explanation: Yes, all 4 angles are right angles.

questions.stem: Which shape has NO right angles?
hints: A circle has no straight corners.

questions.stem: How do you test for a right angle?
hints: You can place a paper square on the angle.
questions.explanation: Use a cut-out square corner to see if it fits perfectly.

questions.stem: How many right angles are in a square?
Does a rectangle have right angles?
options: Yes, all 4 angles are right angles.
hints: Opposite sides are equal, corners are square.
questions.explanation: Yes, all 4 angles are right angles.

questions.stem: How many right angles are in a rectangle?
Use a square corner to test if a door frame forms a right angle. (Teacher assessed).
hints: Hold the paper square to the corner.
questions.explanation: The learner should be able to physically test and state if the angle is right.

criteria.description: States correctly if it is a right angle.

questions.stem: A right triangle has how many right angles?
hints: Think of a triangle with a square corner.

questions.stem: What is the symbol for a right angle?
options: A small square in the corner
A small circle in the corner
A small triangle in the corner
questions.explanation: A small square indicates a right angle.

questions.stem: Look around your classroom. Find one object with right angles and one without. Explain.
hints: Door, book vs a circular clock.
questions.explanation: Example: A book has right angles; a clock has no right angles.

criteria.description: Identifies one object with a right angle.
Identifies one object without a right angle.

questions.misconception: Saying a ball has right angles.

questions.stem: A pupil rotates a right angle so it looks like a V. Is it still a right angle?
options: Yes, the size doesn't change when rotated.
hints: A right angle stays a right angle regardless of orientation.
questions.explanation: Yes, rotating a shape does not change its angles.

questions.stem: A rhombus is a 4-sided shape. Does it always have right angles?
options: No, only if it is a square.
Yes, if it is a rectangle.
hints: Think of a tilted diamond shape.
questions.explanation: No, only a square (which is a special rhombus) has all right angles.
questions.misconception: Saying yes because it has 4 sides.

questions.stem: Explain how to use a piece of paper to test if an angle is a right angle.
hints: Fold the paper to make a square corner.
questions.explanation: Fold the paper so that the two edges meet perfectly. The corner of the folded paper is a right angle. Place it on the angle to test.

criteria.description: Explains folding to create a square corner.
Explains placing it on the angle.

questions.stem: How many right angles does a regular pentagon have?
hints: A regular pentagon has angles of 108 degrees.

questions.stem: Draw a shape with exactly 2 right angles.
hints: Try a trapezoid or a right-angled quadrilateral.
questions.explanation: Any shape with exactly two right angles.

criteria.description: Draws a shape with exactly 2 right angles.

questions.stem: Explain why a parallelogram might NOT have right angles.
questions.explanation: A parallelogram can be slanted, meaning its angles are not 90 degrees (not right angles).

criteria.description: Explains that it can be slanted.

questions.misconception: Thinking all parallelograms have right angles.

questions.stem: A square has 4 right angles. If you cut it in half diagonally, how many right angles are in each triangle?
hints: The cut goes from corner to corner, so the corner angle is split.
questions.explanation: Each triangle has 1 right angle (from the original square).

questions.stem: Design a simple house using shapes. Count and label all the right angles.
hints: Use a square for the body and a triangle for the roof.
questions.explanation: A square body has 4 right angles; the triangle roof may or may not have right angles.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies and labels the right angles.

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.1.1 Analyse the relationships among and between 2-D shapes and 3-D objects according to a variety of attributes, including measurement

skills.description: Identify angles in 2D shapes.
Draw examples of shapes that belong to a given category.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking only sharp corners are angles.
Confusing a shape's corner with an angle's size.

questions.stem: How many angles does a triangle have?
Draw a shape with 4 sides.

criteria.description: Draws a shape with exactly 4 sides.

questions.stem: How many angles are in a square?
Draw a triangle.
Which shape has no angles?
questions.explanation: A circle has no corners or angles.

questions.stem: How many angles does a rectangle have?
How many angles does a pentagon have?
Draw a shape with 5 sides.
Which of these shapes has exactly 4 angles?
How many angles does a hexagon have?
Find and describe an angle in your classroom.
hints: Look at the corner of a table or book.
questions.explanation: Example: The corner of the classroom door forms a right angle.
questions.misconception: Not recognizing angles in real life.

questions.stem: Draw a shape with 6 sides.
How many angles does an octagon have?
Draw a shape with exactly 3 angles.

criteria.description: Draws a shape with exactly 3 angles (triangle).

questions.stem: A pupil says a circle has 1 angle. Is this correct?
hints: A circle has no straight sides or corners.
questions.misconception: Thinking the curve is an angle.

questions.stem: Draw a shape with 3 angles that are all equal.

criteria.description: Draws a triangle with equal sides.

questions.stem: How many angles are inside a quadrilateral?
Draw a complex shape (like a house) and count the total number of angles.
hints: A house has a square body and triangle roof.
questions.explanation: A house shape has 5 angles (4 from the square and 1 at the top of the roof).
questions.misconception: Missing the angle inside the shape.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between a side and an angle in a shape.
hints: Angle is a corner where two sides meet.
questions.explanation: A side is one of the line segments that makes up the shape. An angle is the corner formed where two sides meet.

questions.stem: Look at a 3D cube. How many angles meet at one corner?
hints: Think of the corner of a box.
questions.explanation: 3 angles meet at each corner of a cube.

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.1.1 Analyse the relationships among and between 2-D shapes and 3-D objects according to a variety of attributes, including measurement
indicator.objective: Describe 3D objects according to the shape of the faces, the number of edges and vertices. Sort regular and irregular polygons including triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, heptagons according to the number of sides

skills.description: Identify faces, edges, and vertices of 3D shapes.
Describe the shape of the faces of 3D objects.
Sort 3D objects by faces, edges, or vertices.
Sort regular and irregular polygons by number of sides.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking a cylinder has no edges.

questions.stem: Which 3D shape has 6 square faces?
How many faces does a cube have?
A polygon with 5 sides is called a...
How many edges does a cube have?
hints: Count the edges on a dice.

questions.stem: How many sides does a hexagon have?
How many vertices does a square pyramid have?
hints: 4 at the base and 1 at the top.

questions.stem: What shape are the faces of a rectangular prism?
questions.misconception: Saying squares (only if it's a cube).

questions.stem: Which 3D shape has a curved surface and no straight edges?
How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
Which of these is a regular polygon?
hints: Regular means all sides and angles are equal.
questions.misconception: Saying a rectangle (sides are not all equal).

questions.stem: Describe the faces, edges, and vertices of a cylinder.
questions.explanation: A cylinder has 2 circular faces, 1 curved surface, 2 edges, and 0 vertices.

questions.stem: Sort these objects into two groups based on their faces: sphere, cube, cylinder, pyramid.
hints: Group with flat faces vs curved faces.
questions.explanation: Group 1 (only flat faces): cube, pyramid. Group 2 (has curved faces): sphere, cylinder.

questions.stem: How many edges does a square pyramid have?
hints: 4 at the base + 4 going up to the top.

questions.stem: Which polygon has 7 sides?
A cube and a rectangular prism both have 6 faces. How are their faces different?
options: Cube has all square faces, prism has rectangular faces.
Cube has rectangular faces, prism has square faces.
hints: Cube is a special prism with equal sides.
questions.explanation: Cube faces are all squares; prism faces are rectangles (some might be squares).

questions.stem: A pupil says a cylinder has 3 faces. Is this correct? Explain.
hints: Does the curved surface count as a face?
questions.explanation: Yes, it can be considered to have 3 faces: 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved face.
questions.misconception: Saying no because it has no flat faces on the side.

questions.stem: Draw a regular pentagon and an irregular pentagon.
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides; an irregular one does not.

questions.stem: A cube has 6 faces and 8 vertices. How many edges does it have? Use the formula F + V - E = 2.
Draw a net of a cube.
questions.explanation: A net of a cube is 6 squares arranged so they fold into a cube.

criteria.description: Squares are arranged so they can fold into a cube.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between a regular and an irregular polygon.
hints: What about the sides and angles?
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. An irregular polygon does not.

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.2.1.1 Recognise, create, extend, describe, and use patterns and rules to solve mathematical tasks
indicator.objective: Demonstrate an understanding of increasing and decreasing patterns by extending the next two or three terms and identifying errors or missing elements

skills.description: Identify the rule in a pattern (e.g., add 3, subtract 3).
Extend a pattern by the next 2 or 3 terms.
Create a pattern for a given rule.
Identify errors or missing elements in a pattern and justify.
Locate and describe patterns in a 100s chart.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Not checking the rule against all terms.
Confusing horizontal and vertical patterns on a 100 chart.

questions.stem: What is the next number in the pattern: 3, 6, 9, ___?
What is the rule for the pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20?
questions.misconception: Saying 'add 10' because 10 is in the pattern.

questions.stem: Which number is the error in this pattern: 2, 4, 6, 9, 10?
questions.explanation: 9 is the error. It should be 8.

questions.stem: What is the next number in the pattern: 20, 15, 10, ___?
What is the rule for the pattern: 2, 4, 8, 16?
Extend the pattern by two terms: 12, 16, 20, ___, ___.
questions.explanation: The next two terms are 24 and 28.

questions.stem: Find the wrong number in this pattern: 45, 40, 35, 32, 25.
On a 100 chart, if you move from 24 to 34, what is the rule?
What is the next number in the pattern: 50, 45, 40, ___?
What is the rule for the pattern: 10, 20, 30, 40?
Create a number pattern that adds 6. Write the first four terms.

criteria.description: Creates a pattern with a constant difference of 6.
Shows at least four correct terms.

questions.misconception: Creating a pattern that adds a different number.

questions.stem: Find the error in the pattern: 3, 6, 9, 12, 14.
questions.explanation: 14 is the error. It should be 15.

questions.stem: What is the next number in the pattern: 35, 45, 55, ___?
Find the error and explain: 100, 90, 80, 75, 60.
questions.explanation: 75 is the error. It should be 70. The pattern subtracts 10 each time.

questions.stem: Create a decreasing pattern that subtracts 4. Start at 20.
On a 100 chart, moving diagonally down and right adds 11. If you start at 12, what is the next number?
What is the rule for the pattern: 1, 3, 5, 7?
What is the next number in the pattern: 1, 4, 9, 16, ___?
Find the wrong number in this pattern: 2, 5, 10, 18, 26.
Explain the rule in the pattern: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8.
hints: Look at the last two numbers.
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two previous numbers. 1+1=2, 1+2=3, 2+3=5, 3+5=8.

criteria.description: Explains adding the two previous numbers.

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.4.1. Determine the value of coins and note in order to solve monetary transactions
indicator.objective: Use different denominations of money (1,2, 5, 10, 20, 50 cedis notes an

skills.description: Solve word problems involving money and giving change.
Find different ways to make a given amount using notes.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Forgetting to subtract the cost from the money given to find change.
Using a note value larger than the target amount.

questions.stem: A pencil costs 2 cedis. You pay with a 5 cedi note. How much change do you get?
Which combination makes 10 cedis?
questions.misconception: Thinking only one way is correct.

questions.stem: A book costs 15 cedis. You have a 20 cedi note. How much change?
How many 2 cedi notes make 10 cedis?
Ama buys a pen for 3 cedis and a book for 7 cedis. How much does she spend?
Kojo buys a shirt for 25 cedis. He pays with a 50 cedi note. How much change?
What is the smallest number of notes needed to make 30 cedis using 20, 10, 5 cedi notes?
A trader has 100 cedis. He buys goods worth 45 cedis. How much does he have left?
List two different ways to make 20 cedis using 10, 5, and 2 cedi notes.
questions.explanation: For example: two 10 cedi notes; or one 10 + two 5s.

questions.stem: Ama has 10 cedis. She buys a pen for 3 cedis and a book for 5 cedis. How much does she have left?
How many 5 cedi notes make 50 cedis?
A pupil buys 3 items at 4 cedis each and pays with a 20 cedi note. How much change does he get?
You buy 2 books at 12 cedis each. You pay with a 50 cedi note. How much change?
What is the largest amount you can make using exactly three notes of 10, 20, or 50 cedis?
A family has 100 cedis. They spend 45 cedis on food and 25 cedis on transport. How much is left? Explain.
questions.misconception: Subtracting separately and getting the wrong answer.

questions.stem: A trader sells 5 bags at 10 cedis each. He also sells a basket for 25 cedis. How much does he receive?
Find three different ways to make 50 cedis using 50, 20, 10, and 5 cedi notes.
hints: One 50; or two 20s + one 10; or one 20 + three 10s.
questions.explanation: Examples: one 50; two 20s + one 10; one 20 + three 10s; five 10s, etc.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to buy a toy for 35 cedis. He has saved 10 cedis, 5 cedis, and 2 cedis notes. How many 2 cedi notes does he need to add to reach 35?
You have two 20 cedi notes and three 5 cedi notes. You buy an item for 35 cedis. How much is left?

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.3.1 Develop an understanding of fractions using concrete and pictorial representations and write fractions in words and symbols
indicator.objective: Compare and order unit fractions and fractions with like denominators by using concrete models, pictorial representations and number line.

skills.description: Compare unit fractions (e.g., which is larger, 1/3 or 1/5?).
Compare fractions with the same denominator.
Order fractions from smallest to largest.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Comparing numerators instead of denominators for unit fractions.

questions.stem: Which is larger: 1/2 or 1/4?
hints: Draw a shape cut into 2, and one cut into 4.
questions.explanation: 1/2 is larger because the whole is divided into fewer parts.

questions.stem: Which is larger: 3/5 or 2/5?
Which is larger: 1/3 or 1/6?
Order from smallest to largest: 1/4, 1/2, 1/8. What is the smallest?
Which is smaller: 1/6 or 4/6?
Order from smallest to largest: 2/8, 5/8, 3/8.
Which is larger: 1/5 or 1/10?
hints: Dividing by 5 gives bigger pieces than dividing by 10.

questions.stem: Which is larger: 7/9 or 4/9? Write the numerator of the larger fraction.
Order from largest to smallest: 1/2, 1/4, 1/3.
Order from smallest to largest: 4/10, 1/10, 7/10.
Which is smaller: 2/3 or 2/5?
Explain why 1/8 is smaller than 1/3.
hints: Draw a whole cut into 3 and another into 8.
questions.explanation: When a whole is divided into 8 parts, each part is smaller than when it is divided into 3 parts.

criteria.description: Explains that more parts mean smaller pieces.

questions.stem: Order 5/6, 2/6, 4/6 from smallest to largest and explain your reasoning.
questions.explanation: 2/6 < 4/6 < 5/6 because the numerators are in order 2, 4, 5.

questions.stem: Compare 6/8 and 6/10. Which is larger? Write the denominator of the larger fraction.
A pupil says 1/5 > 1/2 because 5 > 2. Explain the mistake.
hints: Which piece is bigger when cut into 2 vs 5?
questions.explanation: The pupil is confusing larger denominators with larger fractions. 1/2 is larger because dividing into fewer parts makes bigger pieces.

criteria.description: Explains fewer parts means larger pieces.

questions.stem: Which list is ordered from largest to smallest?
Order 3/4, 3/8, 3/2 from smallest to largest. Explain your steps.
hints: Compare denominators: larger denominator = smaller fraction.
2 is smallest denominator, so 3/2 is largest.
questions.explanation: 3/8 < 3/4 < 3/2 because 8 > 4 > 2, and larger denominators mean smaller fractions.

questions.stem: Find a unit fraction that is smaller than 1/4 but larger than 1/10.
Which is larger: 9/10 or 9/12? Write the denominator of the smaller fraction.
hints: Same numerator, larger denominator = smaller fraction.

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.3.1 Develop an understanding of fractions using concrete and pictorial representations and write fractions in words and symbols
indicator.objective: Understand, explain and demonstrate that fractions can be used to represent parts of a group of objects, point on a line, or distances on a number line [Read and write fractions using words and symbols. (E.g. one-half, two halves, thirds, fifths etc.)]

skills.description: Identify a fraction of a group of objects (e.g., half of 6 apples).
Locate a fraction on a number line (e.g., 3/4).
Write fractions in words (e.g., one-half, three-quarters).
Cut a given fraction from a length (e.g., 1/2 of a 12cm stick).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Counting the objects instead of dividing them.
Placing fractions incorrectly on a number line (e.g., 1/4 at the 4 mark).

questions.stem: What is 1/2 of 6 apples?
On a number line from 0 to 1 divided into 4 equal parts, which fraction is at the first mark?
hints: The first mark is 1 part out of 4.

questions.stem: Write 1/2 in words.
hints: Numerator is one, denominator is half.

questions.stem: A stick is 12 cm long. You cut off 1/2 of it. How many cm did you cut?
What is 1/3 of 9 pencils?
A number line from 0 to 1 is divided into 5 equal parts. Where is 3/5 located?
Which of these correctly writes 3/4 in words?
A basket has 10 oranges. What is 1/5 of the oranges?
On a number line from 0 to 1 divided into 8 equal parts, what is the denominator of the fraction at the 5th mark?
A ribbon is 20 cm long. You cut 1/4 of it. How many cm is that?
Explain how to find 1/2 of 8 sweets.
questions.explanation: Divide 8 sweets into 2 equal groups. 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 1/2 of 8 is 4.
questions.misconception: Counting one by one without dividing.

questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is divided into 6 equal parts. What fraction is at the 4th mark?
Write 5/8 in words.
There are 15 pupils in a class. 1/3 of them are girls. How many girls are there?
A rope is 24 m long. You cut 3/4 of it. How many metres did you cut? Explain your steps.
Explain how to locate 2/3 on a number line from 0 to 1.
questions.explanation: Divide the space between 0 and 1 into 3 equal parts. The second mark is 2/3.

questions.stem: Write 'four-fifths' in symbols.
A farmer has 20 goats. He sells 2/5 of them. How many goats did he sell? Explain your reasoning.
Draw a number line from 0 to 2. Mark the point 3/2. Explain where you placed it.
questions.explanation: 3/2 is 1 and a half. It should be halfway between 1 and 2.

criteria.description: Draws a number line from 0 to 2.

questions.stem: A stick is 30 cm long. You cut 2/3 of it. How many cm is the piece left?
